Let \(f\) be a function with \(f(1)=4\) such that for all points \((x, y)\) on the graph of \(f\) the slope is
given by \(\frac{3 x^{2}+1}{2 y}\).
(a) Find the slope of the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x=1\).
(b) Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=1\) and use it to approximate
\(f(1.2)\).
(c) Find \(f(x)\) by solving the separable differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3 x^{2}+1}{2 y}\) with the initial
condition \(f(1)=4\).
(d) Use your solution from part (c) to find \(f(1.2)\).

\begin{itemize}\item[4.] Let \(f\) be a function with \(f(1)=4\) such that for all points \((x, y)\) on the graph of \(f\) the slope is given by \(\frac{3 x^{2}+1}{2 y}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find the slope of the graph of \(f\) at the point where \(x=1\).
\item[(b)] Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at \(x=1\) and use it to approximate \(f(1.2)\).
\item[(c)] Find \(f(x)\) by solving the separable differential equation \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3 x+1}{2 y}\) with the initial condition \(f(1)=4\).
\item[(d)] Use your solution from part (c) to find \(f(1.2)\).
\end{itemize}
\item[(a)] \(\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{3 x^{2}+1}{2 y}\)
\[
\left.\frac{d y}{d x}\right|_{\substack{x=1 \\ y=4}}=\frac{3+1}{2 \cdot 4}=\frac{4}{8}=\frac{1}{2}
\]
\item[(b)] \(y-4=\frac{1}{2}(x-1)\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& f(1.2)-4 \approx \frac{1}{2}(1.2-1) \\
& f(1.2) \approx 0.1+4=4.1
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(c)] \(2 y d y=\left(3 x^{2}+1\right) d x\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
& \int 2 y d y=\int\left(3 x^{2}+1\right) d x \\
& y^{2}=x^{3}+x+C \\
& 4^{2}=1+1+C \\
& 14=C \\
& y^{2}=x^{3}+x+14 \\
& y=\sqrt{x^{3}+x+14} \text { is branch with point }(1,4) \\
& f(x)=\sqrt{x^{3}+x+14}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)] \(f(1.2)=\sqrt{1.2^{3}+1.2+14} \approx 4.114\)
\end{itemize}
